issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task description) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object. Additionally, the StudentCount class exists only in the solution and is not mentioned in the problem or provided in the template. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected return type and whether they must create or use a StudentCount class.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) to match the UML and problem description, removing the StudentCount class; or (b) update the problem statement and template UML/signature to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns a StudentCount and include the StudentCount class or its specification in the template so students know to use it.

issues.description: The problem statement / UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (primitive int) but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object. This introduces a new identifier/type (StudentCount) that is not mentioned in the problem statement or template and changes the expected representation of the same concept (total number of students). Students expecting an int will face mapping confusion when the solution exposes a StudentCount wrapper instead of the primitive type shown in the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Either update the solution to return a primitive int from getTotalNumberOfStudents() (e.g. return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents) so it matches the UML and problem statement, or update the problem statement / UML and template to document the StudentCount type (and its getValue() method) so students are aware that a StudentCount wrapper is used. Prefer the former if the intent is a simple integer total.
